evidence.title: 1968 Australian Championships
evidence.text: The 1968 Australian Championships was a tennis tournament that took place in the outdoor Kooyong Stadium in Melbourne, Australia from 19 to 29 January.

evidence.title: 1968 Australian Championships
evidence.text: It was the 56th edition of the Australian Championships (now known as Australian Open), the 16th held in Melbourne, and the first Grand Slam tournament of the year.

evidence.title: 1968 Australian Championships
evidence.text: It was also the last Grand Slam tournament to be restricted to amateurs.

evidence.title: 1968 Australian Championships
evidence.text: The singles titles were won by Australian William Bowrey and American Billie Jean King.

evidence.title: Ken Rosewall
evidence.text: Kenneth Robert Rosewall {'1': ", '2': ", '3': 'AM, MBE', '4': "} (born 2 November 1934) is a former world top-ranking amateur and professional tennis player from Australia.

evidence.title: Ken Rosewall
evidence.text: He won a record 23 tennis Majors including 8 Grand Slam singles titles and before the Open Era a record 15 Pro Slam titles and a record 35 Major finals overall.

evidence.title: Ken Rosewall
evidence.text: He won the Pro Grand Slam in 1963.

evidence.title: Ken Rosewall
evidence.text: Rosewall won 9 slams in doubles with a career double grand slam.

evidence.title: Ken Rosewall
evidence.text: He is considered to be one of the greatest tennis players of all time.

evidence.title: Ken Rosewall
evidence.text: He had a renowned backhand and enjoyed a long career at the highest levels from the early 1950s to the early 1970s.

evidence.title: Ken Rosewall
evidence.text: Rosewall was one of the two best male players for about nine years and was the World No. 1 player for a number of years in the early 1960s.

evidence.title: Ken Rosewall
evidence.text: He was ranked among the top 20 players, amateur or professional, every year from 1952 through 1977.

evidence.title: Ken Rosewall
evidence.text: Rosewall is the only player to have simultaneously held Pro Grand Slam titles on three different surfaces (1962–1963).

evidence.title: Ken Rosewall
evidence.text: At the 1971 Australian Open he became the first male player during the open era to win a Grand Slam tournament without dropping a set.

evidence.title: Liezel Huber
evidence.text: Liezel Huber (née Horn; born 21 August 1976) is a South African-American retired tennis player who represents the United States internationally.

evidence.title: Liezel Huber
evidence.text: Huber has won four Grand Slam titles in women's doubles with partner Cara Black, one with Lisa Raymond, and two mixed doubles titles with Bob Bryan.

evidence.title: Liezel Huber
evidence.text: On 12 November 2007, she became the co-World No. 1 in doubles with Cara Black.

evidence.title: Liezel Huber
evidence.text: On 19 April 2010, Huber became the sole No. 1 for the first time in her career.

evidence.title: Tennis at the 2012 Summer Olympics
evidence.text: The tennis tournaments at the 2012 Summer Olympics in London were staged at the All England Club in Wimbledon, from 28 July to 5 August.

evidence.title: Tennis at the 2012 Summer Olympics
evidence.text: This was the first Olympic grass court tournament since tennis was reintroduced as an Olympic sport and the first to be held at a Grand Slam venue in the Open era.

evidence.title: Tennis at the 2012 Summer Olympics
evidence.text: (Two other 2012 Summer Olympic bid finalists had also offered Grand Slam venues – second-place finisher Paris offered the French Open venue, the Stade Roland Garros, while fourth-place finisher New York offered the US Open venue, the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing Meadows-Corona Park, Queens.)

evidence.title: 1983 Wimbledon Championships – Women's Singles
evidence.text: Martina Navratilova defeated Andrea Jaeger 6–0, 6–3 in the final to win the Ladies' Singles tennis title at the 1983 Wimbledon Championships.

evidence.title: 1983 Wimbledon Championships – Women's Singles
evidence.text: Billie Jean King became the oldest semi-finalist at a Grand Slam event at 39 years, 7 months and 9 days old, an Open Era record.

evidence.title: 1983 Wimbledon Championships – Women's Singles
evidence.text: Chris Evert's loss in the 3rd round, snapped a streak of 34 consecutive Grand Slam semi-finals, she had made the semi-finals in her first 34 Grand Slam appearances between the US Open 1971 and the French Open 1983.

evidence.title: 1983 Australian Open – Women's Singles
evidence.text: First-seeded Martina Navratilova defeated ninth-seeded Kathy Jordan 6–2, 7–6 in the final to win the Women's Singles title at the 1983 Australian Open tennis tournament.

evidence.title: 1983 Australian Open – Women's Singles
evidence.text: The tournament was played on grass courts at the Kooyong Stadium in Melbourne from 29 November through 11 December 1983.

evidence.title: 1983 Australian Open – Women's Singles
evidence.text: Navratilova earned $75,000 prize money for winning the title, her 8th career Grand Slam singles title and her 2nd title at the Australian Open after 1981.

evidence.title: 1983 Australian Open – Women's Singles
evidence.text: She improved her year record to 86 wins and 1 loss.

evidence.title: 1983 Australian Open – Women's Singles
evidence.text: This tournament was also notable for being the first Australian Open in which Steffi Graf appeared in the main draw, and the last time that Billie Jean King appeared in the main singles draw of a grand slam.

evidence.title: Billie Jean King
evidence.text: Billie Jean King ("née" Moffitt; born November 22, 1943) is an American former World No. 1 professional tennis player.

evidence.title: Billie Jean King
evidence.text: King won 39 Grand Slam titles: 12 in singles, 16 in women's doubles, and 11 in mixed doubles.

evidence.title: Billie Jean King
evidence.text: King won the singles title at the inaugural WTA Tour Championships.

evidence.title: Billie Jean King
evidence.text: King often represented the United States in the Federation Cup and the Wightman Cup.

evidence.title: Billie Jean King
evidence.text: She was a member of the victorious United States team in seven Federation Cups and nine Wightman Cups.

evidence.title: Billie Jean King
evidence.text: For three years, King was the United States' captain in the Federation Cup.

evidence.title: 2010 Aegon Classic – Doubles
evidence.text: Cara Black and Liezel Huber were the two-time defending champions but did not compete together.

evidence.title: 2010 Aegon Classic – Doubles
evidence.text: Black partnered up with Lisa Raymond and Huber with Bethanie Mattek-Sands.

evidence.title: 2010 Aegon Classic – Doubles
evidence.text: Black and Raymond won in the final after Huber and Mattek-Sands retired.

evidence.title: 2005 French Open – Women's Doubles
evidence.text: First-seeded defending champions Virginia Ruano Pascual and Paola Suárez defeated second-seeded Cara Black and Liezel Huber to win the title for the fourth time (after 2001, 2002 and 2004).

evidence.title: 2005 French Open – Women's Doubles
evidence.text: It was their 29th doubles title together, of which eight were won at Grand Slam tournaments.
